text:
Abstract  
We queried the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) for Series accession GSE309890 to (i) summarise the study’s purpose, design and metadata, and (ii) list every downloadable supplementary file that contains the processed expression data. GEO’s geo_series tool was invoked with list_files = true, which retrieves both the E-utilities summary and a directory listing of the FTP “suppl” folder that hosts the files. One record (UID 200309890) was returned, classified as a Series (GSE). The study involves RNA-seq profiling of Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 during adaptive evolution in the presence of the antidepressant sertraline and matched controls (6 samples, platform GPL24659). One compressed CSV file (510 KB) is available for download: “GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz” from the GEO FTP server. No PubMed article is yet linked to the record, suggesting the work is unpublished or not yet indexed. This single file is the sole repository of processed expression values; raw read data must be sought via the linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA/ENA if required.

I. Introduction  
Background.  Selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors (SSRIs) such as sertraline have been implicated in promoting antibiotic resistance in bacteria. Understanding the transcriptional re-wiring underlying this effect can reveal metabolic vulnerabilities for reversing resistance.  
Literature Review.  No literature was retrieved for this query (GEO record not yet linked to PubMed).  
Knowledge Gap.  Prior to this query, the available processed data files for GSE309890 and the study’s experimental details were unspecified.  
Objective & Hypothesis.  Determine the study scope and identify all downloadable expression files for GSE309890; expect exactly the files listed in GEO’s supplementary directory.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design.  GEO was chosen because GSE309890 is a GEO Series accession. The geo_series tool provides both metadata and file inventory.  
Materials.  Database: GEO (via Entrez gds). Tool: geo_series.  
Procedures.  
1. Call geo_series(accession = “GSE309890”, list_files = true).  
   Server constructs esummary on db = gds, id = 200309890, then lists FTP path “…/GSE309890/suppl/”.  
Statistical Analysis.  No statistical operations were required; counts are literal from the server response (sample_count = 6, supplementary_files length = 1).

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Key metadata returned for GSE309890.  
| Field | Value |  
| accession | GSE309890 |  
| title | Antidepressant sertraline biases… |  
| organism | E. coli K-12 MG1655 |  
| assay type | RNA-seq (expression profiling by HTS) |  
| samples | 6 |  
| platform | GPL24659 |  
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |  
| PubMed link | none |  

Table 2. Downloadable supplementary files.  
| File name | Size | URL |  
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510 KB | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

Findings.  GEO lists exactly one processed-data file (compressed CSV of FPKMs) totalling 510 KB. No other matrices, raw FASTQ, or metadata files are present in the suppl directory.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation.  GSE309890 supplies RNA-seq FPKM values for six E. coli samples evolved ± sertraline, suitable for downstream differential-expression analysis.  
Context.  The absence of a PubMed link indicates the study may still be in pre-publication. Users needing raw reads should follow BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA/ENA.  
Limitations.  GEO’s API exposes only processed data; any additional normalisation files or scripts are not archived. Study dates and sample titles are submitter-supplied.  
Conclusion & Future Directions.  Researchers can download the single FPKM matrix to explore sertraline-induced transcriptional shifts. Future work: fetch raw runs via PRJNA1363958 and perform re-assembly or alternative quantification.

References  
[1] GEO Series record GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO FTP directory for supplementary files. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/  

Acknowledgments  
Data were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and stored on the NCBI public FTP server.
